They published Three Worlds together in 1877, but when Barbour denied the ransom in 1878, Russell broke with him.
people.note: Year of birth worked out from his being nearly 30 years older than Russell; year of death from general histories.
events: Russell reads his Herald of the Morning and meets him in Philadelphia
Writes an article denying that Christ's death atones for sin

people.name: Brooke Foss Westcott
people.summary: A British Bible scholar who worked with Fenton Hort for nearly 30 years, comparing manuscripts to restore the original Greek text. Their New Testament in the Original Greek (1881) was consulted for the New World Translation.
events: Publishes The New Testament in the Original Greek with Hort

people.name: Fenton John Anthony Hort
people.summary: A Bible scholar born in Dublin who taught at Cambridge until his death. With Brooke Westcott he published The New Testament in the Original Greek in 1881.
events: Publishes The New Testament in the Original Greek with Westcott

people.name: Joseph Bryant Rotherham
people.summary: A British Bible scholar whose Emphasised Bible (1897) used the form "Yahweh." In his later Studies in the Psalms, published after his death, he went back to "Jehovah," because the familiar form makes the divine name easy to recognize.
people.note: Birth and death years from general histories.

people.name: Maria Russell
people.summary: She married Charles Taze Russell in 1879. Flattery later fed her pride. She left him in 1897 and in 1903 published a tract that misrepresented him; opposers later used statements struck from her court case to slander him. At his funeral in 1916 she laid flowers on his casket, addressed "To My Beloved Husband."
people.note: Birth and death years from general histories.
events: Publishes a tract misrepresenting her husband
Pays her respects at her husband's funeral

people.name: Charles Taze Russell
people.summary: A businessman of Pittsburgh who formed a Bible-study group in 1870. He and his friends learned that the soul is mortal, upheld the ransom, and taught that Christ's presence would be invisible. He started the Watch Tower magazine and pointed to 1914 as the end of the Gentile Times.
events: Born in Allegheny, now part of Pittsburgh
Forms a Bible class in Pittsburgh
Publishes the first volume of Millennial Dawn
The Photo-Drama of Creation is shown to millions
Dies while on a preaching tour

people.name: Joseph Rutherford
people.role: Lawyer; second president of the Watch Tower Society
people.summary: A lawyer who served as the Watch Tower Society's legal counsel and helped arrange its move to Brooklyn. After Russell died he was chosen president.
events: As legal counsel helps arrange the move to Brooklyn
Is chosen president of the Watch Tower Society

people.name: Nathan H. Knorr
people.role: Third president of the Watch Tower Society; Governing Body member
people.summary: Chosen president a few days after Rutherford died, he took the lead in the work for 35 years. He put the stress on training: a school for public speaking in every congregation and Gilead School to train missionaries.
events: Is baptized; Frederick Franz gives the baptism talk
Is chosen the third president of the Watch Tower Society, aged 36
Suggests a school to train missionaries; Gilead School opens the next year
Dies; Frederick Franz is chosen president after him

people.name: Frederick W. Franz
people.role: Fourth president of the Watch Tower Society; Governing Body member
people.summary: A university student who gave up training to be a Presbyterian minister to preach with the Bible Students. He worked on the Society's publications for decades, served as vice president from 1945 and as president from 1977 until he died at 99.
events: Is baptized, and the next year leaves university to preach full-time
Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn
Becomes vice president of the Watch Tower Society
Is the first to chair the Governing Body when the chair starts to rotate yearly
Is chosen the fourth president of the Watch Tower Society

people.name: Thomas J. Sullivan
people.role: Governing Body member; head of the Service Department
people.summary: Born in Ireland, he oversaw the Service Department at headquarters for many years and regularly visited Witnesses jailed in the United States for their neutrality. He was one of the eleven members of the Governing Body when he died.
events: Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn with his wife, Evelyn
Becomes a director of the Watch Tower Society
Dies at 86 as one of the eleven members of the Governing Body

people.name: John O. Groh
people.summary: A trained metallurgist who took up full-time preaching with his wife, Helen. At headquarters he became chief purchaser and helped run many large conventions in New York and elsewhere.
events: Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn
Is one of the ten members already on the Governing Body when it is enlarged
Dies after 41 years of devoted service

people.name: Grant Suiter
people.role: Secretary-treasurer of the Watch Tower Society; Governing Body member
people.summary: He met the Bible Students as a boy in California through the talk 'Millions Now Living Will Never Die.' He served as the Society's secretary-treasurer for 36 years and on the Governing Body.
events: Hears of the Bible Students in California, aged 14
Becomes secretary-treasurer of the Watch Tower Society
Dies months after a severe spinal injury

people.name: Lyman A. Swingle
people.summary: Raised in a Bible Student family in Salt Lake City, he served at headquarters for almost 71 years: in the ink room, on the writing staff and in the Treasurer's Office. He attended a Governing Body meeting a week before he died at 90.
events: Begins serving at headquarters in Brooklyn
Dies at 90, still serving on the Governing Body

people.name: William K. Jackson
people.summary: Known to thousands simply as 'Bill,' he worked with the legal counsel Hayden Covington in the court cases that won many freedoms for Jehovah's Witnesses before the U.S. Supreme Court.
events: Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn
Begins working with Hayden Covington on legal cases
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: George D. Gangas
people.summary: Remembered for his love of righteousness and of Bible questions, which he would put to anyone he talked with. He was in full-time service for 66 years and on the Governing Body for almost 23.
events: Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn
Becomes a member of the Governing Body

people.name: Milton G. Henschel
people.summary: He became Nathan Knorr's secretary as a young man and travelled with him to over 150 lands. In Liberia he was mistreated for refusing a patriotic ceremony, yet went back months later to ask the president for freedom of worship.
events: Is mistreated at a convention in Liberia for refusing a patriotic ceremony
Is one of the ten members already on the Governing Body when it is enlarged

people.name: W. Lloyd Barry
people.summary: A New Zealander with a science degree who served at the Australia branch and then for 25 years as a missionary in Japan, where there were only a dozen preachers when he arrived.
events: Starts full-time service at the Australia branch
Arrives in Japan as a missionary
Is appointed to the Governing Body while branch overseer in Japan
Dies while serving at a convention in Hawaii

people.name: John C. Booth
people.summary: A dairy farmer's son from New York State who pioneered in the rural South, then visited congregations as a traveling overseer, facing mobs, courts and jail. He served at Kingdom Farm for 28 years.
events: Is assigned to Kingdom Farm near Ithaca, New York
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: Charles J. Fekel
people.summary: Born in Bohemia, he knew he had found the truth when he heard Charles Taze Russell speak. He oversaw the composition department of the Brooklyn factory for more than 50 years.
events: Begins serving at headquarters in Brooklyn
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: Karl F. Klein
people.summary: Born in Germany and raised near Chicago, he loved music and played the cello in the Society's radio orchestra. He worked in the Writing Department for half a century.
events: Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: Theodore Jaracz
people.summary: He entered full-time service at 17 and spent nearly 67 years in it, as a Gilead graduate, a traveling overseer and branch servant in Australia.
events: Attends the seventh class of Gilead School
Is invited to join the Governing Body

people.name: Albert D. Schroeder
people.summary: He left engineering studies for full-time preaching, oversaw the work in Britain, and helped write the course for Gilead School, where he taught missionaries for years.
events: Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn
Is sent to oversee the work in Britain
Is deported from Britain and helps prepare the course for Gilead School
Begins serving on the Governing Body

people.name: Daniel Sydlik
people.summary: Jailed in World War II for his neutrality, he then served at headquarters for almost 60 years. He was known as down-to-earth and approachable, and for his love of life.
events: Joins the headquarters staff in Brooklyn
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: Carey W. Barber
people.summary: Born in England and baptized in Canada, he went to Brooklyn with his twin brother to help the Society print its own books. He later visited congregations in the western United States and served on the Governing Body for 30 years, until he died at 101.
events: Moves to Brooklyn to help print the Society's books
Becomes a traveling overseer in the western United States
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: John E. Barr
people.summary: Born in Aberdeen, Scotland, to anointed parents, he overcame his shyness to preach from house to house at 14. He served at the London Bethel and then on the Governing Body for 33 years.
events: Starts preaching from house to house with his father, aged 14
Joins the Bethel family in London
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: Martin Poetzinger
people.summary: A pioneer from Munich who was sent to Bulgaria, Hungary and Yugoslavia, then spent nine years in Dachau and Mauthausen for refusing to give up his faith.
events: Is sent to look after the preaching in Bulgaria
Is sent to a Nazi concentration camp, the year he marries
Is freed and reunited with his wife, Gertrud
Is appointed to the Governing Body

people.name: Gerrit Lösch
people.summary: Born in Austria, he lost his father in World War II when he was about two. He served as a circuit and district overseer in Austria and at the Vienna branch, which oversaw the work in several East European lands.
events: Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Samuel F. Herd
people.summary: Born in a log cabin in Liberty, Indiana, he learned the truth after army service. He and his wife, Gloria, spent over 30 years in the circuit and district work.
events: Begins over 30 years of circuit and district work
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: M. Stephen Lett
people.summary: He served at Bethel as a young man, then with his wife, Susan, as a special pioneer and for nearly 20 years as a circuit overseer.
events: Marries Susan and becomes a special pioneer
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Guy H. Pierce
people.summary: A family man whose warm smile and humour drew people to him. After raising a family he and his wife, Penny, pioneered and spent 11 years in the circuit work.
events: Begins 11 years as a circuit overseer
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: David H. Splane
people.summary: Born in Calgary, Canada, during World War II, he studied music before choosing the full-time ministry. A Gilead graduate, he served as a missionary in Senegal and for 19 years in the circuit work in Canada.
events: Serves as a missionary in Senegal
Joins the Bethel family in the United States
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Geoffrey W. Jackson
people.summary: Born in Queensland, Australia, he pioneered from 15. With his wife, Jenny, he spent 24 years as a missionary in Tuvalu, Samoa and Fiji, where they also translated Bible publications.
events: Is baptized in the Queensland outback
Begins missionary service in Tuvalu, later Samoa and Fiji
Moves to Translation Services in the United States
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Anthony Morris III
people.summary: He served as an operating-room technician in the Vietnam War and fell seriously ill there; later he took up the truth his mother had once studied. He pioneered with his wife, Susan, served where the need was greater, and later did circuit work.
events: Arrives in Vietnam as an army operating-room technician
Joins the Bethel family at Patterson
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Mark Sanderson
people.summary: Raised in San Diego, California, he pioneered in Canada, served as a special pioneer in Newfoundland and on the Philippines Branch Committee.
events: Is appointed to the Philippines Branch Committee
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Kenneth Cook, Jr.
people.summary: From south-central Pennsylvania, he learned the truth from a classmate just before finishing high school. He served at Bethel for over 30 years, in the printery, the office and the Writing Correspondence Department.
events: Begins Bethel service at Wallkill, New York
Becomes a helper to the Writing Committee
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Gage Fleegle
people.summary: Raised in western Pennsylvania, he set the goal of Bethel service at 12. He served at Bethel from 1991, in the Bindery, the Service Department and the Teaching and Service committee offices.
events: Becomes a helper to the Service Committee
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Jeffrey Winder
people.summary: Raised in Murrieta, California, he began pioneering months after his baptism. At Bethel he helped build the world headquarters at Warwick.
events: Begins Bethel service at Wallkill, New York
Helps build the world headquarters at Warwick
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Jody Jedele
people.summary: Raised in the truth in Missouri, he served at Bethel, learned Spanish, and later left Bethel for some years to care for his parents.
events: Is baptized in his early teens
Begins Bethel service at Wallkill, New York
Returns to Bethel for the Warwick construction project
Is added to the Governing Body

people.name: Jacob Rumph
people.summary: Raised in California, he asked for a Bible study at 13. He pioneered from high school and in 2000 moved to Ecuador to serve where the need was greater.
events: Moves to Ecuador to serve where the need is greater
Is added to the Governing Body
His tribute to Shalmaneser III of Assyria is pictured on the Black Obelisk

augustus.note: Birth from his age at death, 76 years.
events: As Octavian, defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
Forgives Herod for backing Antony and enlarges his kingdom
Is proclaimed 'Augustus' and rules as emperor
Orders the registration that brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem
His temple relief at Karnak lists 156 towns he took in the land, even the 'Field of Abram'
Hundreds of flood legends from six continents and the islands echo the Flood
Babylonian temple-towers carry inscriptions like 'its top shall reach the heaven,' as at Babel
Digs show that Ur, the city he left, was then at the height of its power
Tablets from Nuzi show the same custom of a childless man adopting an heir, as he planned with Eliezer
The titles, names and customs in his account fit the Egypt of his day exactly
Jericho shows a terrible destruction by fire, and the site lay empty for generations
Hazor, 'the head of all these kingdoms,' covered some 60 hectares, digs show
An old water tunnel from the Gihon spring may explain how Jerusalem was taken
Remains at Hazor from his time suggest a chariot city
The Moabite Stone gives King Mesha's side of Moab's revolt and names Omri and Jehovah
His annals, found in his palace at Khorsabad, claim the capture of Samaria
The Siloam Tunnel, cut through rock from Gihon, bears an inscription about its digging
